prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported concussion. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1005; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound on a multi-lane arterial in Sugar Land, Texas, when the vehicle ahead slowed for traffic. Driver 2 was following Driver 1 and did not stop in time, striking the rear of Driver 1's vehicle with considerable force. A Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle at the time of impact. Officers on scene interviewed both drivers and the Passenger, and independent witnesses who stopped at the location gave statements consistent with what the drivers described. Driver 2 acknowledged following too closely and did not dispute the sequence of events. Photographs taken at the scene show the rear damage to Driver 1's vehicle and the position of both vehicles after impact. Driver 1 reported being dazed immediately after the collision and was later evaluated by medical staff for a suspected concussion, a finding that fits the nature and force of this type of impact. Officers noted that Driver 1's vehicle had no visible earlier damage, and Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Some of the damage observed to the vehicle's interior and undercarriage may not have resulted from this collision alone, and the extent to which it did cannot be determined from the scene evidence.
